designation.ap3_enterprise_issuer: Cloudflare Access, team 'ugence', backed by Google Workspace (Workspace domain ugence.ai); non-production Access application 'AP3 Enterprise Issuer Validation' on the validated hostname ap3-validation-endpoint.rakeshmohan888.workers.dev (ap3-validation.ugence.ai is a planned custom hostname, currently blocked by DNS/zone configuration, not operational and not live-validated; AP3-D6); policy 'Google Workspace group' (Allow) admitting ugence-ap3-test@ugence.ai; test principal ap3-test@ugence.ai. accounts.google.com is the login method behind Access, not the application JWT issuer
designation.jwks_trust: configured JWKS endpoint https://ugence.cloudflareaccess.com/cdn-cgi/access/certs (IA-3: no OIDC discovery; default TLS verification; keys cached by kid, refreshed once on an unknown kid, then fail closed)
designation.token_type_profile: AP3-D1 CLOUDFLARE_ACCESS_PROFILE, AMENDED 2026-09-11 on live evidence: the adapter's issuer_profile 'cloudflare-access' admits a JOSE header with typ absent (the live Access token carries alg and kid only, per evidence.live_token_capture) and, when typ is present, only the exact value 'JWT' (case-insensitive per RFC 7515); it requires alg exactly RS256 (narrower than IA-2), a recognized kid, successful signature verification against the designated JWKS, the exact issuer, the exact audience and all temporal checks. The absent typ is never permission for alg none, an unsigned token, an unknown algorithm or a missing/unknown kid. IA-1 (typ at+jwt) is unchanged for the default profile and every other issuer profile. Original ruling (typ exactly JWT) recorded in ADR section 20.7; amendment in the same section
designation.tenant_claim: AP3-D2 STATIC_ISSUER_AUDIENCE_MAPPING: Cloudflare Access supplies no top-level tenant claim and none is invented. For this profile only, tenant_id = 'ugence.ai' (AdapterConfig.bound_tenant), selected by the exact trusted pair iss = https://ugence.cloudflareaccess.com and aud containing 24b3008ed1910d53caebbaffb3358aa801bd9dc5cf9f5af8aa7ada87335b12b3, and accepted only when the verified email, after NFC normalization and trimming, has the domain exactly 'ugence.ai' (AdapterConfig.verified_email_domain; domain compared case-insensitively, local part as presented). The email suffix corroborates the binding and is not the source of the tenant identity; a wrong issuer, wrong audience, absent email or non-ugence.ai email fails closed (ISSUER_MISMATCH, AUDIENCE_MISMATCH, ACTOR_SHAPE_AMBIGUOUS, EMAIL_DOMAIN_MISMATCH). This is a static mapping, not permission to derive tenants from email domains
designation.principal_claim: sub (the Access user's stable issuer-scoped identifier); email is the IdP-verified human-readable address and a directory-binding attribute, never the key
designation.actor_type_claim_or_mapping: AP3-D3 CLAIM_SHAPE_MAPPING: HUMAN iff signature and every token constraint hold, sub is present and non-empty, email is present and under the verified domain, and no service-token marker (common_name) is present. Service token (recorded as the port's non-human kind SYSTEM, subject = common_name, no tenant bound) iff common_name is present and non-empty with an empty or absent sub and no email [I]. Any mixed, incomplete, conflicting or ambiguous shape is refused ACTOR_SHAPE_AMBIGUOUS (fail closed). This is an explicit owner-ratified adapter mapping for this profile, not an inference from sub; the Cloudflare claim type='app' names the application-token class and never classifies the actor
designation.directory_binding: the Authority Directory principal_id is the issuer-qualified subject reference percent-encoded(iss)|percent-encoded(sub) (ID-2); the verified email is recorded as the display and binding attribute; the Cloudflare Access Google-group policy is admission evidence, never a substitute for an internal role grant (AX-5)
designation.transport_header_boundary: AP3-D4: AW-3 stands; the write gate reads X-Ugence-Approver-Proof (WRITE_PROOF_HEADER) first and unchanged. Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion is the Cloudflare-facing transport header only: governed_runtime_worker.cloudflare_access_boundary.CloudflareAccessProofBoundary reads it through an adapter configured with the cloudflare-access profile, validates the token completely and emits the plane's normalized ApproverIdentity; the raw header never reaches the gate, is never copied into X-Ugence-Approver-Proof and is never stored or echoed. The boundary is a default-off argument of build_authority_writes; composition.py does not construct it (production wiring deferred)
designation.writer_authorizer_for_rows_14_to_16: AP3-D5: build_authority_writes accepts a default-off writer_authorizer conforming to the RA-6 WriterAuthorizer seam and refuses a reference authorizer under production=True. Rows 14 to 16 run with tests/_conformance_authorizer.py (label TEST_ONLY_CONFORMANCE_AUTHORIZER_NOT_AX5, is_reference_authorizer=True) over the real adapter, the real gate and the real SqliteAuthorityDirectory. This is not production AX-5, which stays sequenced after AP-3 (section 19.5); composition.py composes no authorizer
designation.jwks_rotation_behaviour: Cloudflare publishes the current and next signing keys at the certs endpoint and rotates them on its own schedule [I]; the adapter refreshes the JWKS exactly once on an unknown kid and retries verification once, then refuses KEY_UNKNOWN; a JWKS that cannot be fetched is IdentityUnavailable, never an unauthenticated answer; an unsigned payload is never decoded
designation.planned_custom_hostname: ap3-validation.ugence.ai (planned; blocked by DNS/zone configuration; not operational; not live-validated)
designation.production_validation_scope: human identities authenticated through the designated Google Workspace group ugence-ap3-test@ugence.ai (AP3-D6); Cloudflare service identities are not commissioned for production; their token-shape handling is covered by conformance tests only
